The land here is working ALR farm land with barns and a farm residence, not bare building lots.

Abbotsford farm ground covers the whole city, not one neighbourhood. The City is 389 square kilometres and about 72% of its land is in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR).
Sumas Prairie is the main eastern farm block. The City describes it as a 90 square-kilometre area of low-lying, highly productive agricultural land in East Abbotsford.

Matsqui Prairie and Bradner-Mt. Lehman are the other named prairie farm areas in City material. AgRefresh background work grouped contraventions by Bradner-Mt. Lehman, Matsqui Prairie, Aberdeen-South Poplar and Sumas Prairie.

The farm stock here is working farms, not houses on lots. The City calls Abbotsford one of the most intensively and diversely farmed areas in Canada, supporting a wide range of crop and livestock production.

Farm dwellings sit inside that working fabric. The Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) frame allows generally one principal residence per ALR parcel, plus one additional residence only where the parcel qualifies.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Farms: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The ALR rules govern most Abbotsford farm purchases.
A secondary suite is allowed only inside the principal residence.
City zoning still applies on top of the ALR frame. The City directs buyers to check current zoning, future land use and development permit areas through its property information search or WebMap.

Outside the ALR, a secondary suite must be inside the principal unit, registered, and less than 50% of the principal unit, and a coach or garden suite may use up to 15% of the lot to a maximum of 100 square metres.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Farms: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Flood recovery is nearly complete but long-term protection is not finished. The City states all major recovery projects are complete or underway, including the Cole Road Dike, Sumas River bank stabilization and North Parallel Road Dike repairs, while phase two design for the Barrowtown Pump Station floodwall is underway.

The Barrowtown Pump Station matters to Sumas Prairie farms. The City states phase one of its new floodwall is complete, and the wall is intended to reduce the risk of the station not operating during a major Nooksack overflow event.

A joint flood plan is being built with neighbours and First Nations. The Province states the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative brings together Semá:th and Leq'á:mel First Nations, Abbotsford, Chilliwack and British Columbia to reduce flood risk in the watershed.

Highway 1 runs through the flood area. The City states flooding in Sumas Prairie threatens Highway 1, the Trans Mountain Pipeline, the Westcoast Energy pipeline, the Sumas-Huntingdon border crossing and Southern Railway service.
Farm income proof must be kept.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Farms: development and new projects

items.t: The City states that after the 2021 flood it commissioned a full post-flooding analysis of Sumas Prairie to protect First Nations communities, businesses, residents and agricultural properties, forming the foundation of its Long-Term Flood Mitigation Plan.

The City has applied to exclude ALR land for a sports park, with ALR land offered in return. The City states it submitted an exclusion application to the ALC for a recreation and sports park at King and McKenzie Roads, and offered two City-owned parcels totalling about 50 acres on LeFeuvre Road for inclusion in the ALR.
Farm land is taxed as BC Assessment Class 9 only when it qualifies.

Leased farm land has its own filing rule. BC Assessment states a copy of a current lease must be submitted, a new lease is required on expiry, and resubmission is required every seven years to keep farm classification on leased land.
The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) taxable area includes Abbotsford.
City property taxes were due July 2, 2026. The City states a first 5% penalty applied July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on September 16, 2026.

Highway 1 is the main farm-to-market road. The Fraser Valley Express, Route 66, connects Chilliwack and Abbotsford with Langley and Burnaby via Highway 1, as the Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) describes it.
Route 66 is a daily interregional service. BC Transit lists Route 66 Fraser Valley Express as serving Chilliwack, Abbotsford, Langley and Burnaby with daily service, operated by Chilliwack Transit.
The Sumas-Huntingdon border crossing is inside the farm area's risk picture. The City names that crossing among the critical infrastructure threatened by Sumas Prairie flooding.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Farms: risks and due diligence

items.t: Flood is the first check on any Sumas Prairie parcel. The City states Sumas Prairie has a long history of flooding from Nooksack River overflow, most notably in 1990 and 2021, so buyers should confirm dike protection and flood construction requirements for the lot.

Check the parcel's zone and plan designation before assuming a farm use is allowed. The City states current zoning, future land uses and development permit areas can be found through its property information search or WebMap.

Check ALR status and residence limits on the ALC record. The ALC states local governments may further regulate or restrict residences in the ALR, so City zoning and the ALC frame both need reading for the same parcel.

faq.a: AgRefresh rewrote the farm rules buyers now work under. The City says it completed AgRefresh, a three-stage process that reviewed agricultural policies, bylaws and regulations and set a compliance framework for ALR land, updating Official Community Plan policy and Zoning Bylaw regulation for farming areas, so a buyer should check the current bylaw position, not an older listing description.
faq.q: What did AgRefresh change for farm buyers?

faq.a: Sumas Prairie floods from across the border, not just local rain. The City states overflow from the Nooksack River at Everson, Washington flows north into Sumas Prairie, with major events in 1990 and 2021, so buyers there need the dike, pump station and flood construction position for the specific parcel, not a city-wide assumption.
faq.q: Why is Sumas Prairie flood risk different from other Abbotsford farms?

faq.a: No, farm class must be applied for and earned. BC Assessment requires a producing farm to meet minimum gross income at farm gate prices — $2,500 on an operation of 0.8 to 4 hectares, $2,500 plus 5% of actual value above 4 hectares, and $10,000 under 0.8 hectares — with applications due October 31.
faq.q: Does buying ALR land give me farm tax class automatically?

faq.a: Under the ALC frame: one principal residence of 500 m² or less (no more than 1,000 m² of fill), a secondary suite only within the principal residence, and at most one additional residence of up to 90 m² on properties 40 ha or less or up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha, with local government rules possibly more restrictive.
faq.q: What residence can an Abbotsford ALR farm have?

faq.a: BC Assessment's thresholds are $2,500 for an operation of 0.8 ha to 4 ha, $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha for a larger operation, and $10,000 for an operation under 0.8 ha; applications are due by October 31 for the next tax year, and a buyer continuing to farm must apply by October 31 after purchase.
faq.q: What income must a farm operation show to keep farm classification?

faq.a: For a City of Abbotsford parcel: all property taxes were due July 2, 2026 by midnight, with a first 5% penalty on July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty on September 16, 2026.
